newsitem.title: UK: BT hails end to UK govt's "golden share".
newsitem.headline: BT hails end to UK govt's "golden share".

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Tuesday said it was very pleased the UK government was willing to cancel a "golden share" it has held in the company since privatisation.
"We see this as a final step in disengaging from formal government control," a spokeswoman said.
The "golden share" has only a nominal value but allowed the government to prevent BT from making any changes in its articles of association.

Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary Margaret Beckett said on Tuesday the government was now prepared to end the arrangement. BT was partially privatised in 1984 and the remainder of the company was floated in 1991.
The "golden share" meant the government could prevent any shareholder from owning more than 15 percent of the company or block the appointment of a non-Briton as BT executive chairman.

The BT spokeswoman said that either of these scenarios would still require a change in the articles of association and the approval of 75 percent of shareholders. She stressed that BT had no plans to amend its articles.

The spokeswoman said there was no direct link with BT's planned merger with MCI Communications Corp of the United States. But she said the continuing nominal government involvement had caused some confusion among BT's many overseas partners.
